# Language reference

This catalogue is the same metadata used by Language Server hover help. For runnable
programs, use the [validated example inventory](examples.md).

## `???`

Typed hole placeholder for incomplete code.

```funscript
??? [optionalMessage]
```

A hole placeholder that satisfies any type at compile time but raises a diagnostic or throws an uncatchable defect at runtime if reached. Ideal for rapid prototyping.


See also: `never`.

## `<`

Numeric less-than comparison.

```funscript
number < number
```

Native ordering operators are available only when both operands are proven numbers. Compare strings and domain values with an explicit Effect Order.


See also: `Order.isLessThan`, `String.Order`.

## `<-`

Effect bind operator inside effect blocks.

```funscript
binding <- effectExpression
```

Extracts the success value from an Effect within an `effect` block, short-circuiting on failure. Desugars to `yield*` in `Effect.gen`.


See also: `effect`, `Effect`.

## `<=`

Numeric less-than-or-equal comparison.

```funscript
number <= number
```

Native ordering operators are available only when both operands are proven numbers. Compare strings and domain values with an explicit Effect Order.


See also: `Order.isLessThanOrEqualTo`, `String.Order`.

## `=>`

Function, match arm, and explicit return arrow.

```funscript
(param: Type) => body
```

Expression-bodied functions return their expression. Function and effect blocks end with an explicit `=> value`; match arms use `=>` to introduce their result.


See also: `effect`.

## `>`

Numeric greater-than comparison.

```funscript
number > number
```

Native ordering operators are available only when both operands are proven numbers. Compare strings and domain values with an explicit Effect Order.


See also: `Order.isGreaterThan`, `String.Order`.

## `>=`

Numeric greater-than-or-equal comparison.

```funscript
number >= number
```

Native ordering operators are available only when both operands are proven numbers. Compare strings and domain values with an explicit Effect Order.


See also: `Order.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo`, `String.Order`.

## `|>`

Pipeline composition operator.

```funscript
expression |> function(args...)
```

Passes the value of the left expression as the first argument (or into placeholder `_`) of the right expression. Compiles to `pipe(...)` or direct function invocation. Bare companion operations resolve only when the source proves a companion module. If multiple companions expose the name and the source is unproven, compilation reports the explicit namespaces to choose from.

Untrusted dictionaries and payloads can be safely decoded directly using `payload |> decode(TargetSchema)`.


See also: `pipe`, `Effect.map`, `Effect.timeout`.

## `and`

Logical short-circuit conjunction operator (&&).

```funscript
expr1 and expr2
```

Evaluates to `true` if both operands are truthy. Short-circuits if the left operand is falsy. FunScript uses the English word `and` instead of `&&`.


See also: `or`, `not`.

## `Array`

Ordered sequence of elements of type T.

```funscript
type Array<T>
```

Standard sequence collection. In FunScript, Arrays are deeply immutable unless operated on inside an explicit `mut` draft. Compatible with Effect's `Array` module combinators (`Array.map`, `Array.filter`).


See also: `Chunk`, `Record`, `mut`.

## `boolean`

Primitive boolean logic type.

```funscript
type boolean = true | false
```

Represents logical truth values (`true` or `false`).


See also: `true`, `false`, `and`, `or`, `not`.

## `Chunk`

High-performance, immutable indexed sequence from Effect.

```funscript
type Chunk<A>
```

A fast, persistent sequential data structure with O(1) prepend, append, and slice operations, optimized for streaming and batch processing.


See also: `Array`.

## `Context`

Type-safe environment container for service tags and instances.

```funscript
type Context<Services>
```

Represents the dependency environment `R` in `Effect<A, E, R>`.


See also: `service`, `Layer`.

## `DateTime`

Immutable representation of an absolute point in time.

```funscript
type DateTime
```

Effect's modern date-time module replacing JavaScript's mutable `Date`.


See also: `Duration`.

## `default`

Exports an expression as the default export of the module.

```funscript
export default <expression>
```

Specifies the default export of a module or route file.

Only one default export is permitted per file. Useful for framework integrations (e.g. Next.js, Remix, Vite) and route components.


See also: `export`, `import`.

## `Duration`

Representation of an elapsed time interval.

```funscript
type Duration
```

Effect's type representing a time duration, constructed with `Duration.millis`, `Duration.seconds`, `Duration.minutes`, etc. Used for timeouts, delays, and scheduling.


See also: `Schedule`, `DateTime`.

## `effect`

Introduces an effectful computation block with generator semantics.

```funscript
effect
  result <- effectfulCall
  _ <- logCall
  => result
```

Delimits an Effect workflow that compiles to `Effect.gen(function* () { ... })`. Bind effects with `<-`, discard results with `_ <-`, and finish with `=> value`. Early exits and errors use typed Effect operations.


See also: `Effect`, `service`, `fail`, `<-`.

## `Effect`

Core Effect type representing a lazy, concurrent computation.

```funscript
type Effect<Success, Error = never, Requirements = never>
```

The foundational abstraction in FunScript.

An `Effect<A, E, R>` represents a blueprint for a workflow that:
- Requires an environment/context `R`
- May fail with a typed error `E`
- May succeed with a value `A`

Effects are lazy, composable, cancellable, and fibers-based.


See also: `service`, `effect`, `Layer`, `Context`.

## `Effect.all`

Executes multiple Effects concurrently or sequentially and combines results.

```funscript
Effect.all(effects: Array<Effect<...>>, options?: { concurrency?: number }): Effect<Array<...>>
```

Gathers multiple effects into a single Effect that collects all success values in an array or struct.


See also: `Effect.forEach`.

## `Effect.andThen`

Sequentially composes effects or functions.

```funscript
Effect.andThen<A, B>(self: Effect<A, E, R>, next: Effect<B, E2, R2> | ((a: A) => B)): Effect<...>
```

Versatile combinator that chains an Effect or a pure function after another Effect succeeds.


See also: `Effect.map`, `Effect.flatMap`.

## `Effect.catchAll`

Recovers from any error in the Effect's error channel.

```funscript
Effect.catchAll<A, E, R, B, E2, R2>(self: Effect<A, E, R>, handler: (err: E) => Effect<B, E2, R2>): Effect<A | B, E2, R | R2>
```

Catches all typed errors in `E` and invokes a recovery function that returns an alternative Effect.


See also: `Effect.catchTag`, `fail`.

## `Effect.catchTag`

Recovers from a specific tagged error matching _tag.

```funscript
Effect.catchTag(tag: string, handler: (err: Tagged) => Effect<...>): Effect<...>
```

Selectively catches errors matching a specific discriminant tag (from `error` schemas). Leaves all other errors intact in the `E` channel.


See also: `error`, `Effect.catchAll`.

## `Effect.die`

Halts fiber execution immediately with an unrecoverable defect.

```funscript
Effect.die(defect: unknown): Effect<never>
```

Terminates the current fiber with an uncatchable defect (system bug or assertion failure).


See also: `Effect.orDie`, `fail`.

## `Effect.flatMap`

Chains another Effectful computation onto the success of this Effect.

```funscript
Effect.flatMap<A, B, E2, R2>(self: Effect<A, E, R>, f: (a: A) => Effect<B, E2, R2>): Effect<B, E | E2, R | R2>
```

Sequentially composes two Effectful actions where the second depends on the result of the first.


See also: `Effect.map`, `Effect.andThen`.

## `Effect.forEach`

Iterates over an iterable, applying an effectful function to each element.

```funscript
Effect.forEach(elements: Iterable<A>, f: (a: A) => Effect<B, E, R>, options?: { concurrency?: number }): Effect<Array<B>, E, R>
```

Replaces imperative loops for effectful iteration. Can run sequentially or concurrently using the `concurrency` option.


See also: `Effect.all`.

## `Effect.fork`

Spawns an Effect onto a new concurrent background fiber.

```funscript
Effect.fork<A, E>(self: Effect<A, E, R>): Effect<Fiber<A, E>, never, R>
```

Starts background execution of an Effect in an isolated green fiber.


See also: `Effect.forkScoped`.

## `Effect.forkScoped`

Forks a fiber bound to the current Scope's lifetime.

```funscript
Effect.forkScoped<A, E>(self: Effect<A, E, R>): Effect<Fiber<A, E>, never, R | Scope>
```

Spawns a fiber that is automatically interrupted and cleaned up when the enclosing Scope closes.


See also: `Effect.fork`, `Effect.scoped`.

## `Effect.map`

Transforms the success value of an Effect using a pure function.

```funscript
Effect.map<A, B>(self: Effect<A, E, R>, f: (a: A) => B): Effect<B, E, R>
```

Applies the mapping function `f` to the successful result of `self` without altering errors or dependencies.


See also: `Effect.flatMap`, `Effect.andThen`.

## `Effect.orDie`

Demotes all typed errors in E into fatal defects.

```funscript
Effect.orDie<A, E, R>(self: Effect<A, E, R>): Effect<A, never, R>
```

Converts recoverable errors in the `E` channel into defects, asserting that the operation cannot fail.


See also: `Effect.die`.

## `Effect.repeat`

Repeats a successful Effect according to a Schedule policy.

```funscript
Effect.repeat(policy: Schedule): Effect<...>
```

Repeatedly executes an Effect as long as the Schedule allows.


See also: `Schedule`, `Effect.retry`.

## `Effect.retry`

Retries a failing Effect according to a Schedule policy.

```funscript
Effect.retry(policy: Schedule): Effect<...>
```

Automatically re-executes an Effect upon failure until the schedule policy dictates termination.


See also: `Schedule`, `Effect.repeat`.

## `Effect.runPromise`

Runs an Effect at the application boundary, returning a Promise.

```funscript
Effect.runPromise<A, E>(effect: Effect<A, E, never>): Promise<A>
```

Evaluates the Effect workflow to completion and resolves the resulting Promise with the success value. Only permitted in application entrypoints (`main`).


See also: `Effect.runSync`.

## `Effect.runSync`

Synchronously executes an Effect that cannot fail and has no requirements.

```funscript
Effect.runSync<A>(effect: Effect<A, never, never>): A
```

Executes an Effect synchronously. Throws if the Effect contains asynchronous fibers or unresolved failures.


See also: `Effect.runPromise`.

## `Effect.scoped`

Provides a new Scope to an Effect and closes it upon completion.

```funscript
Effect.scoped<A, E, R>(self: Effect<A, E, R | Scope>): Effect<A, E, R>
```

Creates an execution boundary for resources requiring deterministic cleanup (like files or sockets).


See also: `Effect.forkScoped`, `Layer.scoped`.

## `Effect.succeed`

Creates an Effect that succeeds immediately with the provided value.

```funscript
Effect.succeed<A>(value: A): Effect<A>
```

Wraps a pure value in an Effect that succeeds synchronously without errors or dependencies.


See also: `Effect.fail`, `Effect.sync`.

## `Effect.sync`

Wraps a lazy, synchronous side effect into an Effect.

```funscript
Effect.sync<A>(evaluate: () => A): Effect<A>
```

Defers execution of a synchronous function until the Effect is run, capturing any uncaught throws as defects.


See also: `Effect.succeed`, `Effect.tryPromise`.

## `Effect.timeout`

Enforces a maximum execution time on an Effect.

```funscript
Effect.timeout(duration: Duration): Effect<Option<A>>
```

Aborts the Effect if it does not finish within the specified duration.


See also: `Duration`.

## `Effect.tryPromise`

Bridges an asynchronous Promise-based API into a typed Effect.

```funscript
Effect.tryPromise<A, E>(options: { try: () => Promise<A>, catch: (err: unknown) => E }): Effect<A, E>
```

Safely converts external Promise calls into FunScript Effects. Catches Promise rejections and maps them into typed domain errors in the `E` channel.


See also: `Effect`, `effect`.

## `error`

Declares a typed error schema backed by Schema.TaggedError.

```funscript
error ErrorName(field: Type, ...)
```

Defines a domain error with a discriminator `_tag` matching the error name.

Because errors are typed values rather than unchecked runtime exceptions, they appear explicitly in the `E` channel of `Effect<A, E, R>` and can be matched by tag.


See also: `fail`, `schema`, `Effect.catchTag`.

## `export`

Exports a binding, schema, error, service, or default value from the module.

```funscript
export declaration = ...
export schema Name = ...
export service Name ...
export default <expression>
```

Exposes module members to other files. Supports both named exports (`export name = value`) and default exports (`export default expr`).


See also: `import`, `default`.

## `extern`

Retired language construct.

```funscript
extern (Retired)
```

The 'extern' keyword has been retired under FunScript's Strict Zero-Alias Policy in favor of native 'service' declarations and explicit 'js' interop inside layer implementations.


See also: `service`, `js`, `Layer`.

## `fail`

Constructs an Effect that fails with a recoverable typed error.

```funscript
Effect.fail(error: E): Effect<never, E, never>
# in effect block:
_ <- Effect.fail(ErrorType(reason))
```

FunScript eliminates unchecked exceptions, `throw`, and `try/catch`. All recoverable failures are modeled as typed values in the Effect `E` channel.

`fail` (or `Effect.fail`) produces an Effect that terminates execution along the error channel. Callers must handle the typed error exhaustively using `match`, `Effect.catchTag`, or `Effect.catchAll`.


See also: `effect`, `error`, `Effect.succeed`, `Effect.catchTag`.

## `false`

Boolean literal representing falsehood.

```funscript
false: boolean
```

The primitive boolean value representing false.


See also: `true`, `boolean`.

## `from`

Specifies the module source in import and export declarations.

```funscript
import { X } from "module"
```

Specifies the source file path or npm package name for `import` and `export { ... } from` statements.


See also: `import`, `export`.

## `HashMap`

Persistent immutable hash map data structure from Effect.

```funscript
type HashMap<K, V>
```

Efficient immutable hash map with structural hashing and equality.


See also: `Record`, `HashSet`.

## `HashSet`

Persistent immutable set data structure from Effect.

```funscript
type HashSet<A>
```

Efficient immutable collection of unique elements with structural hashing and equality.


See also: `HashMap`.

## `import`

Imports bindings, services, types, or schemas from another module.

```funscript
import { Name } from "module"
```

Static ESM imports support named, default, namespace, side-effect-only, and type-only forms. Module specifiers must be non-interpolated strings.


See also: `export`, `from`.

## `Int`

Refinement schema constraining numbers to 32-bit integers.

```funscript
schema Int = number |> Schema.int()
```

A refined numeric schema that validates numbers to be whole integers without fractional parts.


See also: `number`, `schema`.

## `js`

JavaScript and npm interop keyword for typed async interop.

```funscript
res <- js promiseFn()
export js fn = (...) => ...
eff |> js
```

Lifts JS Promises into Effects inside effect blocks (`res <- js promiseFn()`). Native throws and rejections become the typed `JsInteropError` channel. When TypeScript declares the resolved value as `A | null | undefined`, js converts it to `Option<A>` with `Option.fromNullishOr`; non-nullable values remain `A`. An `any`, `unknown`, or unresolved native result becomes `Option<Unknown>`, requiring both absence handling and schema validation. It also compiles exported functions to Promise-returning JS functions (`export js fn`) and pipes Effects to JS Promises (`eff |> js`).


See also: `ts`, `effect`, `export`.

## `Layer`

Recipes for constructing, composing, and providing services.

```funscript
type Layer<Out, Error = never, In = never>
```

A `Layer<Out, E, In>` specifies how to construct services `Out` given dependencies `In`. Layers enable modular dependency injection, memoization, parallel construction, and resource management.


See also: `service`, `Layer.succeed`, `Layer.effect`.

## `Layer.effect`

Builds a Layer that constructs a service via an Effect.

```funscript
Layer.effect<T, E, R>(tag: Service<T>, build: Effect<T, E, R>): Layer<T, E, R>
```

Allows effectful setup (e.g. connecting to a database, reading config) when instantiating a service.


See also: `Layer`, `Layer.succeed`, `service`.

## `Layer.scoped`

Builds a Layer with managed lifecycle and resource cleanup.

```funscript
Layer.scoped<T, E, R>(tag: Service<T>, build: Effect<T, E, R | Scope>): Layer<T, E, R>
```

Binds the constructed service to a Scope. The service will be automatically torn down when the layer is released.


See also: `Layer`, `Effect.scoped`.

## `Layer.succeed`

Builds a Layer that provides a service with a static implementation.

```funscript
Layer.succeed<T>(tag: Service<T>, implementation: T): Layer<T>
```

Supplies a pre-constructed service implementation directly without asynchronous setup.


See also: `Layer`, `Layer.effect`, `service`.

## `match`

Unified pattern matching and conditional branching construct.

```funscript
match value
  | Pattern1 => result1
  | Pattern2 when guard => result2
  | _ => fallback
```

`match` is the sole branching construct in FunScript, replacing `if`, `else`, and `switch`.

Features:
- Exhaustive structural pattern matching on tagged variants, literals, records, and arrays (via `ts-pattern`).
- Compile-time exhaustiveness checking when the wildcard `_` arm is omitted.
- Subjectless boolean branching (`match | condition => expr | _ => default`).
- Pattern guards via `when` and or-patterns via `| A | B =>`.


See also: `variant`, `when`, `schema`.

## `mut`

Declares a local mutable draft or mutable variable.

```funscript
mut draft = initialValue
# or in pipeline:
value |> mut (draft) => draft.field = newValue
```

FunScript bindings and data structures are immutable by default. The `mut` keyword enables explicit, controlled copy-on-write mutation backed by Mutative's `create(...)`.

Rules:
- Local reassignments are only permitted on `mut` bindings.
- Pipeline drafts (`|> mut (draft) => ...`) create isolated draft scopes.
- Top-level `mut` and closure-captured mutable mutation across fibers are prohibited.


See also: `record`, `|>`.

## `never`

The bottom type representing values that never occur.

```funscript
type never
```

Uninhabited type used for functions that never return, effects that cannot fail (`Effect<A, never>`), or unreachable branches in exhaustive pattern matching.


See also: `unknown`, `void`.

## `None`

Represents the absence of a value in an Option.

```funscript
Option.none(): Option<never>
```

Represents an empty `Option` container, replacing `null` and `undefined`.


See also: `Option`, `Some`.

## `NonEmptyString`

Refinement schema validating strings with length greater than zero.

```funscript
schema NonEmptyString = string |> Schema.nonEmptyString()
```

Guarantees at compile and run time that a string contains at least one character.


See also: `string`, `schema`.

## `not`

Logical negation operator (!).

```funscript
not expression
```

Inverts a boolean expression. Evaluates to `true` if the expression is falsy, and `false` otherwise. FunScript uses `not` instead of `!`.


See also: `and`, `or`.

## `number`

Double-precision IEEE 754 floating point and integer numeric primitive.

```funscript
type number
```

Represents all numbers in FunScript, including floating-point values and integers. Can be refined to integers via `Int` schema.


See also: `Int`, `string`, `boolean`.

## `Option`

Data type modeling the presence or absence of a value.

```funscript
type Option<A> = Some<A> | None
```

FunScript disallows `null` and `undefined`. Optional values are represented strictly with `Option<A>` from Effect, containing either `Some(value)` or `None`. Eliminates null pointer exceptions.


See also: `Some`, `None`, `Result`.

## `or`

Logical short-circuit disjunction operator (||).

```funscript
expr1 or expr2
```

Evaluates to `true` if either operand is truthy. Short-circuits if the left operand is truthy. FunScript uses the English word `or` instead of `||`.


See also: `and`, `not`.

## `pipe`

Chains values through functions from left to right.

```funscript
pipe(value, f1, f2, ...): Result
```

Utility function for data-first function composition. In FunScript, the `|>` pipeline operator is preferred syntax and compiles down to `pipe` calls.


See also: `|>`.

## `record`

Declares an immutable record schema or constructs an immutable record.

```funscript
schema Name = { field: Type }
# or expression:
{ key: value, ...spread, path.nested: value }
```

FunScript records are deeply immutable by default.

Record updates support shallow spread (`{ ...user, age: 37 }`) and deep nested dot-path updates (`{ ...order, shipping.carrier: "DHL" }`). Deep updates compile to Mutative's structural-sharing `create(...)` to guarantee both performance and purity without manual nested spreads.


See also: `schema`, `mut`, `variant`.

## `Record`

Dictionary map of keys to values.

```funscript
type Record<K extends string | number | symbol, V>
```

Key-value dictionary mapping string keys to values of type `V`.


See also: `HashMap`, `record`, `Array`.

## `Ref`

Fiber-safe concurrent mutable reference cell.

```funscript
type Ref<A>
```

Effect's primitive for shared, concurrent state across fibers. All read and write operations (`Ref.get`, `Ref.set`, `Ref.update`) return Effects, ensuring atomic and lock-free thread safety.


See also: `effect`, `Effect`.

## `Result`

A value representing either success or failure.

```funscript
type Result<A, E> = Success<A, E> | Failure<A, E>
```

Use `Result.succeed(value)` and `Result.fail(error)` when success and failure must remain available as data.


See also: `Option`, `Effect`.

## `Schedule`

Recurrence policy defining repetition and retry behavior.

```funscript
type Schedule<Env, In, Out>
```

Configures delays, intervals, exponential backoffs, and iteration bounds for `retry` and `repeat`.


See also: `Effect.retry`, `Effect.repeat`, `Duration`.

## `schema`

Unified declaration for record shapes, tagged unions, refinements, and type signatures.

```funscript
schema Name = { field: Type }
# or tagged union:
schema Name = | CaseA | CaseB(v: Type)
```

Declares data models backed by Effect's `@effect/schema` and `Data.TaggedEnum`.

A single `schema` declaration generates both the runtime validator/constructor and the static TypeScript type definition, avoiding dual declaration boilerplate. Untrusted payloads and dictionaries can be safely decoded using `payload |> decode(Name)`.


See also: `record`, `variant`, `error`.

## `service`

Declares a dependency-injected service interface.

```funscript
service ServiceName
  methodName: (param: Type) => Effect<Success, Error>
```

Defines a service contract that compiles to an Effect `Context.Service` tag.

Calls to service methods (such as `UserRepo.find(id)`) inside `effect` blocks automatically resolve the service from Context and track its dependency in the Effect `R` channel. Implementations are supplied at runtime via `Layer.succeed`, `Layer.effect`, or `Layer.scoped`.


See also: `Layer`, `Context`, `effect`, `Effect`, `js`.

## `Some`

Constructs an Option containing a defined value.

```funscript
Option.some<A>(value: A): Option<A>
```

Represents the presence of a value in an `Option` container.


See also: `Option`, `None`.

## `string`

UTF-16 text string primitive type.

```funscript
type string
```

Represents immutable textual data. FunScript strings support string interpolation via curly brace syntax `"{status}: {message}"` and multiline string literals.


See also: `NonEmptyString`, `number`, `boolean`.

## `true`

Boolean literal representing truth.

```funscript
true: boolean
```

The primitive boolean value representing true.


See also: `false`, `boolean`.

## `ts`

TypeScript escape hatch for complex declarations, expressions, and types.

```funscript
schema Dict = ts { Record<string, unknown> }
type Position = ts { import('vscode-languageserver').Position }
```

Embeds verbatim TypeScript in a balanced `ts { ... }` block without expanding FunScript's core grammar. Useful for generics, utility types, and third-party library types.


See also: `js`, `schema`.

## `unknown`

The type-safe counterpart of any; represents an uninspected value.

```funscript
type unknown
```

Top type representing values whose type is not statically known (e.g. from external API payloads). Must be narrowed via `raw |> decode(TargetSchema)` or `match` before access.


See also: `never`, `schema`.

## `UUID`

Refinement schema validating RFC 4122 compliant UUID strings.

```funscript
schema UUID = string |> Schema.UUID
```

Validates and types canonical UUID strings (such as `123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000`).


See also: `string`, `schema`.

## `variant`

Declares a tagged union variant constructor within a schema.

```funscript
schema TypeName =
  | VariantA(param: Type)
  | VariantB
```

Declares a variant case of a discriminated union algebraic data type.

Under the hood, variants compile to Effect `Data.TaggedEnum` and `Schema.Union`. Each variant can be instantiated directly as a constructor function (e.g. `Circle(10)`) or constant (`None`) and pattern-matched exhaustively with `match`.


See also: `schema`, `match`, `error`.

## `void`

Represents the absence of a meaningful return value.

```funscript
type void
```

Used as the return type for side-effecting operations that do not produce a useful value, such as `Console.log` or mutating operations yielding `Effect<void>`.


See also: `never`, `unknown`.

## `when`

Pattern match guard condition within a match arm.

```funscript
| Pattern when condition => result
```

Adds a boolean predicate to a `match` arm. The arm matches only if both the structural pattern matches and the `when` condition evaluates to `true`.


See also: `match`.
